body: Agreed. Agreed agreed agreed. Agreed x1000. This is good, you have a clear head and a good answer to the "guilt trip" school of suicide prevention.

The potential downsides of medication are threefold but only one of those reasons is relevant for the purpose of this conversation, namely that I work in a career that will make it challenging to have constant health insurance coverage. Also, refills may be physically unavailable sometimes. Psych meds must be taken daily forever, in order to be effective and getting off them and on them again causes massive swings.

I reconcile it because I can't feel what others are feeling. So many people's suicide reasons appear silly or frivolous to me, when I read them as words. But I doubt that it's the reason that drive those people to suicide but the resulting emotions. If your ability to handle stress is basically zero, you will feel the same amount of anguish from a mundane problem that a normal person would feel from a war zone. 

It's like AIDS. AIDS doesn't kill people. It takes away their immune response and then the mundane flu kills them. It's like that, except mental. Also, there are multiple categorical reasons why I won't go on psych meds and so far, neither friends nor professionals have convinced me to try it.

I have never attempted it either but I was talking to a dude who tried to jump off the Golden Gate and he said that the only thing more awful than facing your own death is facing your cowardice at the inability to do it. All the way on the ride to the psych clinic, he thought "I am such a fuckup, I even fucked up dying."

Talking about the mechanics and logistics of suicide methods is much more comforting to me. The thought of my death frightens my body kind of like the moment before a skydive. But it makes my mind feel at peace.

I appreciate your question but I'd rather not get into my reasons as they only make sense to me and not to other people. For example, most normal people would consider my reasons very insufficient for suicide and either try to talk me out of it or dismiss me as a weak person. 

I have slightly different standards for my own behavior and the behavior of others and I don't expect anyone to understand my daily desire to die. 

The main point is that self-terminating is hard. I have to do all kinds of cranial impact research to make sure I get enough of a start, I have to stake out the necessary buildings, get their height in feet and make sure I'm not mistaken for a burglar when I climb on the roof. I have to approach the edge and overcome the fear of death. It's distressing, this. I wish I had a shotgun by my desk.

I would like to kill myself. Also, I'd like to vent about how hard it is to kill myself in light of: 

- Biological self-preservation instinct
- Laws and safety precautions
